sections.title: The Appointment of the Seven
observations: In this section, we see the early church facing a practical problem: the distribution of food to widows. The apostles recognize that their primary calling is to prayer and the ministry of the Word, so they decide to appoint seven men to oversee this task.

The selection of these seven men is significant. They are described as being of good repute, full of the Spirit and wisdom. This highlights the importance of character and spiritual maturity in church leadership.
This decision reflects a model of shared leadership and delegation, which is essential for the growth and health of the church.

sections.title: The Ministry of Stephen
observations: Stephen, one of the seven appointed, begins to perform great wonders and signs among the people. His ministry is marked by the power of the Holy Spirit, demonstrating that God is at work through him.
Opposition arises from members of the Synagogue of the Freedmen, who dispute with Stephen. This illustrates the ongoing conflict between the early church and the established religious authorities.
Stephen's ability to speak with wisdom and the Spirit highlights the importance of being filled with the Holy Spirit in our witness and ministry.

sections.title: Stephen's Speech and Martyrdom
observations: Stephen is brought before the Sanhedrin, where he delivers a powerful speech recounting Israel's history and God's faithfulness. He emphasizes the rejection of God's messengers, culminating in the rejection of Jesus.
His speech serves as a bold proclamation of the gospel and a call to repentance for the Jewish leaders. It also foreshadows the persecution that the church will face.

Stephen's martyrdom is a pivotal moment in Acts, as it marks the beginning of widespread persecution against the church, leading to the scattering of believers and the spread of the gospel beyond Jerusalem.

importantVerses.commentary: The apostles instruct the church to select men of good repute, full of the Spirit and wisdom, emphasizing the qualities necessary for church leadership.
Stephen's wisdom and the Spirit's presence in his speech highlight the divine empowerment for ministry and witness.
The reaction of the Sanhedrin to Stephen's speech reveals the hardness of their hearts and the consequences of rejecting God's message.

questions: What does the appointment of the seven reveal about the structure and leadership of the early church?
How does Stephen's ministry exemplify the role of the Holy Spirit in the life of a believer?
What can we learn from Stephen's response to persecution and his boldness in proclaiming the gospel?
